text:
alex: quick thread — I did a short assay to reproduce the regression after the kernel switch on Mixtral. seeing worse tail latency for MQA workloads. paste results below, need ideas on kernel selection + kv layout for GQA vs MQA.

jon: can you drop the raw numbers?

alex: pasted. baseline = mixtral-v1 kernels (old). current = mixtral-auto-kernel. workload = chat-ish, 2-streams, kv-cache warmed.

alex: 
```
BENCH SUMMARY (local rig: A100 40GB)
scenario | p50 | p95 | throughput (req/s)
mixtral-v1-default | 9.8 ms | 36 ms | 275
mixtral-auto-kernel | 11.9 ms | 52 ms | 210
mixtral-kernel-force-mha | 10.5 ms | 41 ms | 245
gqa-layout (num_kv_heads=32, kv_dim=64) | 10.8 ms | 44 ms | 230
mqa-layout (num_kv_heads=64, kv_dim=128) | 13.7 ms | 68 ms | 180

notes: p95 regression concentrated on MQA with paged layout, fragmentation spikes when many short queries intermixed.
```

maya: interesting — looks like the auto kernel picks a vectorized path that increases memory pressure in KV paged mode. did you track GPU mem alloc patterns?

alex: yes. saw recurring 1-2MB allocations every few tokens and extra memcpy spikes in timeline. likely due to kernel using an intermediate buffer per head.

perf-bot: CI: perf/regressions detected on mixtral-8k (branch: runtime-kernel-sel). latency +12% p95 on workload "chat-mqa-small". See: https://perf.redwood/reports/1792345600

sam: fyi i repro'd with a small harness. swapping to the older MHA kernel + enabling head-packing fixes the memcpy churn. proposing a conservative heuristic: prefer MHA kernel when num_kv_heads * kv_dim > 4096 OR when rope_scale != 1.0 for Mixtral/Qwen.

lee: can you show the heuristic as a config change?

sam: sure — config snippet i tested: 
```
kernel_selection:
  prefer_mha_if:
    kv_product_gt: 4096
    rope_scale_not_1: true
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  dynamic_window_ms: 6
kv_cache:
  layout: paged
  page_size_kv_dim: 256
  fragmentation_guard: 0.07
```

jon: fragmentation_guard = fraction of page occupancy to trigger compaction?

sam: yes, if free fraction > 7% we compact the page into a fused buffer; helps MQA where many heads leave small holes. compaction cost measured ~0.6ms per page but reduces memcpy spikes overall.

maya: what about RoPE scaling? we had earlier notes that >1.0 causes extra compute for rotary transforms which interacts with kernel choice.

alex: confirmed. when rope_scale=1.2 we see extra matmul/rot overhead and combined with MQA high kv dims it amplified p95. forcing kernel with in-place rotary gave better p95.

lee: for GQA (fewer kv heads, larger kv_dim) the auto kernel seems fine — throughput wins. so heuristic should be model-aware: GQA -> prefer auto; MQA -> fallback to MHA/in-place kernels and consider compaction.

jon: any quick tests on Qwen baseline?

alex: ran Qwen-7B/rope-scale 1.0: auto kernel = good. Qwen-7B/rope-scale 1.4: p95 +20% with paged layout. same fix (in-place rotary + pack heads) restores parity.

sam: I'll open a patch that: (1) adds kernel selection heuristic, (2) adds fragmentation_guard with tunable threshold, (3) exposes a telemetry tag for "kv_frag_events".

alex: thanks. next steps: sam open PR, run CI perf suite with MQA-rich prompt set, we should sweep fragmentation_guard in {0.03,0.07,0.12} and kv_product_gt in {2048,4096,8192}.

maya: ping me on the PR — i'll run the A/B on dedicated pools. :+1:

lee: i can write a small microbench to simulate many short queries hitting paged KV to tune compaction cost vs benefit.

alex: awesome. tagging summary for folks joining later: kernel vs KV-layout interaction is root cause; RoPE scale magnifies effect; proposed fixes = kernel heuristic + page compaction + head-packing; experiments scheduled.

alex: will update thread with PR link and CI dashboard once available.
